card.text: Explore the DART encounter shape of Didymos and its radial heights.

introduction.text: Didymos is the rapidly rotating primary of the near-Earth binary visited by DART and LICIACube in 2022. Its broad equatorial ridge and flattened poles are reconstructed from their images. Its moon Dimorphos was the target of DART’s asteroid-deflection experiment. Explore the published shape, radial heights and derived relative surface brightness.

shape.title: SPC shape model v003
shape.summary: An image-based shape model. Smooth regions lack image coverage; no surface photograph is mapped.

draco.title: DART approach photographs
draco.summary: Two DRACO frames from 158 and 94 seconds before impact: one wider view and one closer partial view. Brightness is approximately normalized; photographed shadows remain. Grid marks unobserved or rejected areas.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: Height relative to a 365 m sphere, including the ridge. Smooth regions have weaker image constraints.

albedo.title: Relative-albedo model
albedo.summary: Grayscale shows modeled brightness, not absolute albedo. Accepted facets cover about 58% of the shape; the grid marks the rest.
